myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, the world was entirely silent of reflection. When a bird sang, the sound simply vanished into the ether. A young spirit named Aurelia lived in the deep canyons of the world, tasked with weaving the wind. She was lonely, for the wind only howled and never spoke back.

One evening, Aurelia caught a falling star in her silver net. The star, desperate to return to the heavens, offered her a wondrous gift in exchange for its release: a sliver of eternity. Aurelia agreed, but instead of keeping it for herself, she shattered the sliver against the canyon walls.

The magic seeped into the cold stone. From that day on, the rocks remembered. When Aurelia called out into the canyon, the stone called back, its voice a perfect reflection of her own. She was never lonely again.

The other spirits marvelled at this beautiful new magic. They named the phenomenon "Echo," after the ancient word for memory. Even today, when you shout into a valley or a deep cave, you are hearing the canyon's ancient promise to Aurelia, ensuring that no wandering voice in the vast wilderness is ever truly left entirely alone anymore.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, there lived a gentle wind spirit named Aella. Aella loved the earth, but she was entirely invisible. While the river could show its sparkling blue waters and the forest could flaunt its emerald leaves, Aella had nothing to show the world but the rustling of others.

One evening, feeling deeply unnoticed, Aella wept into the grand canyon of the highest peaks. A solitary mountain giant, carved of granite and deep slumber, awoke to her sorrow. Pitying the unseen spirit, the giant offered her a gift. "I cannot give you a body," he rumbled, "but I can give you a reflection."

The giant inhaled deeply and blew a magical frost over the canyon walls, turning the stone into perfect acoustic mirrors. When Aella spoke again, the mountains answered, bouncing her voice from peak to peak until it filled the valley. Her pure joy was so great that she laughed, and the mountains laughed with her.

To this day, if you call out among the high rocks, Aella will eagerly catch your words and toss them back to you. Mortals call it an echo, but it is truly the invisible spirit, finally making herself known.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long ago, the wind was a nameless wanderer, howling across the earth but leaving no trace. Aella, a lonely spirit of the deep canyons, loved the wind’s fleeting songs but wept when silence inevitably returned. She longed for a way to make the beautiful sounds linger.

One night, as a meteor shower rained across the heavens, Aella climbed the highest peak and caught the falling silver dust in a net woven from moonbeams. She didn't keep the celestial magic for herself. Instead, she painted the steep granite walls of her canyon with the glowing stardust, whispering a spell of memory into the cold stone.

When the wind next rushed through the valley, singing its wild, invisible song, the stardust flared. The canyon walls caught the sound in their magical embrace and tossed it back, perfectly mimicking the wind's voice. The mountains had learned to speak.

Aella was never lonely again. The wind, delighted to finally hear its own voice, visited the canyon often to play. Mortals who wander into these deep, rocky valleys today call this lingering voice an echo, unaware they are hearing the ancient magic of stardust remembering the wind.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the valleys learned to sing, the world was a place of fading moments. Every joyful shout, every sorrowful cry, and every bird’s melody simply dissolved into the endless sky. Zephyr, a solitary watcher of the deep gorges, collected these fleeting sounds in woven baskets of cloud-silk, mourning how quickly they died.

Desiring to preserve the world's voice, Zephyr climbed to the highest peak to seek the wisdom of the slumbering Earth-Shaker. Moved by Zephyr’s quiet dedication, the ancient titan offered him a celestial geode, a hollow stone filled with the shimmering dust of fallen stars. "This is the mirror of time," the titan rumbled. 

Zephyr returned to the deepest canyon and scattered the stardust across the towering cliffs. The granite absorbed the shimmering magic, transforming into vast, unseen tapestries of memory. When Zephyr released his baskets of sound, the cliffs caught the melodies and tossed them back, refusing to let them fade. 

The world was never silent again. Mortals came to call this magic the Echo, unaware that each bouncing call is Zephyr’s ancient stardust at work, faithfully catching our fleeting words and ensuring they dance across the mountains before slipping away.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Before the canyons learned to answer, the world was plagued by silence. Every joyous laugh, every whispered secret, and every wolf’s howl simply melted into the vastness of the sky. Lyra, a gentle guardian of the deep ravines, spent her days gathering these fleeting sounds in jars of spun dawn-light, sorrowful that they vanished so quickly. 

Determined to give the world a lasting voice, Lyra sought out the heart of a fallen comet that had crashed into the highest peak. The celestial stone hummed with the magic of deep space—a mirror of eternity. Grinding the star-core into a shimmering silver dust, she returned to her steep ravines and painted the towering granite walls with the cosmic powder. 

The cold stone drank the stardust and awakened. When Lyra unsealed her jars, releasing a cacophony of saved melodies and shouts, the painted cliffs caught the sounds. Instead of letting them fade, the ravines tossed them back, a perfect, bouncing reflection of life. 

Today, mortals call this phenomenon the Echo. Whenever you call out in a deep valley, you are not just hearing your own voice, but waking Lyra’s ancient stardust, which faithfully refuses to let you be forgotten.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the valleys learned to sing, the mountains stood in absolute, brooding silence. They were eternal but voiceless, forced to watch the ephemeral world dance around them. Every bird’s melody and every joyful shout simply dissolved into the endless sky, leaving the ancient stones as mute witnesses.

Aella, a spirit of the morning mist, pitied the silent cliffs. She spent her days weaving blankets of fog, but she longed to give the mountains the gift of song. When a brilliant comet tore across the heavens, Aella cast her shimmering nets into the sky, catching its trailing, crystalline dust.

She did not keep this celestial magic. Instead, she wove the comet-dust into the very veins of the granite gorges. The magic acted as a bridge between the fleeting and the eternal. The next time a falcon cried out over the abyss, the enchanted stone eagerly caught the sound, holding it for a brief moment before joyously tossing it back into the air.

The mountains finally had a voice, borrowed from the world around them. Today, mortals call this phenomenon an echo, unaware that they are conversing with ancient stone, awakened by the magic of a fallen comet.

myths.Agent_1: Myth: In the earliest days, the great canyons were beautiful but entirely deaf. Kaelen, a solitary shepherd of the high crags, felt the immense weight of this silence. He would play his silver flute to the vast chasms, but the sweet melodies were instantly swallowed by the empty air, leaving him truly alone. Desperate for a companion, Kaelen climbed to the highest summit where the sky touched the earth. There, he discovered the shattered remains of a fallen star, its core still glowing with the vibrant memory of the cosmos. Kaelen gathered the luminous stardust and carried it back down to the headwaters of the great mountain spring. He cast the shimmering powder into the rushing waters. As the enchanted river carved its long way through the deep ravines, it fed the cold granite with celestial magic. The sleeping stone drank the stardust and awakened. The next evening, when Kaelen played his flute, the canyon walls eagerly caught the notes and tossed them back, harmonizing beautifully with his lonely tune. Mortals now call this bouncing sound an echo. They do not realize that whenever they shout into the abyss, they are waking ancient stardust, sharing a beautiful and timeless song.

Mourning how quickly sounds perished in the void, she soared to the highest snowy peak where a brilliant comet had recently shattered. She gathered its celestial core, still humming with the deep magic of the cosmos, and crushed it into a shimmering silver dust.

Realizing that wind alone could not alter ancient stone, Aella carried the glowing stardust into the heart of a massive thunderhead. She spun the heavy clouds until they burst, unleashing a torrential, sparkling rain over the deep ravines. As the enchanted storm battered the cliffs, the heavy celestial drops carved invisible, resonant grooves into the cold granite, awakening the sleeping rock.

When Aella next howled through the canyons, the magical cliffs eagerly caught her voice in their new grooves. Instead of letting it die, the ravines joyously tossed it back. Today, mortals call this an echo, unaware they speak to the stars.

Mortals now call this bouncing sound an echo, unaware that their voices are traveling through ancient star-carved pathways, sharing a timeless song with the earth.

Myth: Before the world learned to answer itself, the great canyons were voids of absolute silence. They were majestic but greedy, swallowing the songs of birds, the roar of rivers, and the cries of beasts without returning a single note.

Aella, a restless spirit of the mountain winds, could no longer bear the heavy quiet of her domain. Seeking a voice for the silent earth, she ascended to the craggy peaks where a wandering comet had recently collided with the world. Aella gathered the shattered, humming stardust, vibrating with the latent energy of the cosmos.

Knowing her winds alone were too soft to change the ancient stone, Aella carried the glowing dust into the belly of a fierce, brewing tempest. Instead of raining it down, she forged the stardust into jagged bolts of celestial lightning. As the storm raged, Aella hurled these brilliant, stardust-infused strikes against the sheer canyon walls. The intense cosmic heat melted the cold granite, fusing it into sweeping, glass-like acoustic arcs.

When the storm cleared and Aella sang her victory down the ravine, the crystallized arcs caught her voice, tossing it back in perfect harmony. Today, mortals call this an echo, unaware they speak to the lightning.

When Orin sang out, the giant instrument caught his voice, plucking it back across the ravine. Mortals now call this bouncing sound an echo, unaware their voices are strumming invisible, star-forged strings.
